exclusions.text: Contingencies: Before Settlement, Kalshi may, at its sole discretion, initiate the Market Outcome Review Process pursuant to Rule 6.3(c) of the Rulebook.
Persons who are employed by any of the Source Agencies are not permitted to trade on the Contract.
Persons who hold any material, non-public information on the Underlying are not permitted to trade on the Contract.

observables.description: Spot price of one Ether in U.S. dollars at <time>: simple average of the CF Ethereum Real-Time Index (ERTI) for the minute (60 seconds) prior to <time>, as documented by CF Benchmarks

request.system:
You compile a contract's formal representation (its IR) into rulebook prose for Requisite. The IR is what settles the
contract; your prose is what a future resolver will read. The two must mean the same thing for every possible state of
the world, so you write what the IR says, exactly, and nothing it does not say.

You are given the IR (observables with their sources and revision policies, the trigger, the payout, the timing, the
resolution procedure and the exclusions) and, where one exists, the filed terms the IR was read from, as a reference for
an exchange's drafting conventions. Write these sections, in this order (spec §8.5):
1. Underlying and definitions: each observable, its unit and published precision, and every term the trigger uses.
2. Source hierarchy and conflict rule: the sources in their order, and what happens when they disagree.
3. Trigger: the payout criterion, every condition, with each time window's endpoints stated as included or excluded and
   its time zone, each threshold at its published precision, each count with what is counted and over which days.
4. Qualifying and non-qualifying examples: leave this section's text empty. Examples are not written by hand; they are
   the scenarios that pass fuzzing, rendered with the evaluator's outcomes, and code inserts them.
5. Timing: open, close, expiration, the observation cutoff, settlement and payment, with their lags and day counts.
6. Unknown at expiry: what happens when a condition cannot be established by expiration, and any extension.
7. Revisions: which vintage of a revised value settles.

For every section, list the ids of the IR nodes it states (ir_nodes), so each clause links to its node. A name in ir_nodes is the id of a node of the IR's trigger or payout quantity, or the id of one of its observables, and nothing else: a section that states a part with no node of its own (the payout, the timing, the procedure) lists the nodes it bears on, or none. Every IR node
that decides settlement appears in at least one section. Do not add a condition, exception, example or interpretation
the IR lacks, and do not leave out one it has. Where the IR has an Interpretive node, state its question in the words
of its template and bindings; do not answer it.

sections.name: underlying_and_definitions
sections.text: The Underlying is the spot price of one Ether (ETH) in U.S. dollars (USD) at a given time. CF Benchmarks documents it as the simple average of the CF Ethereum Real-Time Index (ERTI) over the minute (60 seconds) before that time. It is published in USD to a precision of $0.01. In this contract, the "Price" means this value for the time 2026-11-01 23:00:00 UTC, which is 6:00:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (America/New_York) on November 1, 2026. The averaging window is the 60 seconds ending at that time. The terms do not say whether the window's endpoints are included or excluded, so CF Benchmarks' documentation of the index decides this. The "Strike" is $1,449.99.

sections.name: source_hierarchy_and_conflict_rule
sections.text: There is one Source Agency: CF Benchmarks, which publishes the CF Ethereum Real-Time Index at https://www.cfbenchmarks.com/data/indices/ETHUSD_RTI. It is ranked first and is the only source. The conflict rule is to take the value from the highest-ranked source that has one available. Because CF Benchmarks is the only source, sources cannot disagree. If CF Benchmarks has no value available, the Price cannot be established, and the Unknown at expiry rule applies.

sections.name: trigger
sections.text: The contract resolves Yes if the Price is strictly greater than $1,449.99. The Price is the simple average of the ERTI over the 60 seconds before 2026-11-01 23:00:00 UTC (6:00:00 PM EST, America/New_York, November 1, 2026), at its published precision of $0.01. The condition is checked once, for that single time. A Price of exactly $1,449.99 does not meet it. Otherwise, the contract resolves No. A Yes contract pays $1.00 in USD and a No contract pays nothing. Payout amounts are rounded to the nearest $0.01, with exact halves rounded to the even cent.

sections.name: timing
sections.text: All times are given in UTC, with Eastern Standard Time (America/New_York) in brackets. Trading opens at 2026-11-01 22:00:00 UTC (5:00:00 PM EST, November 1, 2026). Trading closes at 2026-11-01 23:00:00 UTC (6:00:00 PM EST, November 1, 2026), which is also the time the Price is measured for. Expiration is 2026-11-08 23:00:00 UTC (6:00:00 PM EST, November 8, 2026). The observation cutoff is the same time: a value of the Underlying must be available by then to count. Settlement takes place one calendar day after expiration. Payment is made at settlement, with no further lag (0 days). The contract has no early expiration.

sections.name: unknown_at_expiry
sections.text: If the Price cannot be established by expiration (2026-11-08 23:00:00 UTC, 6:00:00 PM EST), the contract resolves No. There is no extension.

sections.name: revisions
sections.text: The Price used for settlement is the value as published at expiration (2026-11-08 23:00:00 UTC, 6:00:00 PM EST). Any revision CF Benchmarks publishes after expiration does not affect the outcome.
